candidate.title: Original Sin of npm: A Study on Vulnerability Propagation in JavaScript Dependency Networks
documentedPopulationConstruction: npm-follower weekly snapshot reported as of 2023-09-05.
3,946,361 packages and 36,432,989 package versions before sampling.
Random sample of 1.5 million package names followed by live-registry availability and stub filtering.
1,077,946 parent packages in the resulting analysis database.
candidate.documentedOutcome: Disclosed OSV/NVD vulnerability propagation and lifecycle information.

blockingConditions: The documented target is vulnerability propagation, not closed-world malicious-publication or maintainer-compromise coverage.
The reported parent population was altered through live-registry availability and stub filtering after sampling, so it is not a frozen cutoff-valid at-risk population.
The paper describes a custom database build but does not supply a named downloadable row-level release, filtered export, or query endpoint for that database.
The paper does not define a pre-registered future non-event observation horizon for its sampled population.
permittedUse: Methodology context for vulnerability introduction, publication, fixing, and right-censoring discussions only.
prohibitedInterpretations: Do not treat vulnerability absence as a benign or uncompromised npm control label.
Do not treat the reported sample as an accessible frozen population for this benchmark.
Do not fit or evaluate malicious-publication or maintainer-compromise ranking, calibration, PR-AUC, Recall@K, logistic-regression, blast-radius, or attack-return models from this source.
